cues.en: In this lecture, we are going to talk about the first step of problem solving.
So it's obvious that many people nowadays learn coding.
But the biggest challenge for new developers is problem solving, because everyone can learn programming
language syntax and start writing code by copying other people's code, or remake an application following
step by step instruction.
But the hardest thing has to do with solving new problems and new challenges.
It's very crucial to have a strong problem solving skill set.
As I mentioned, a lot of it will naturally come by practicing, so it's worth having a plan to follow
step by step to become a better problem solver.
We have mentioned our recipe in our previous lecture, so we will start with our first step, which
is to understand the problem.
So imagine you are sitting in a room, there is an interviewer ahead of you and she or he asks a question
and you don't know how to solve it.
So this is not a problem that you have seen before, and it is the first time you are facing this challenge
over here.
So in this case, without panicking, the first thing you should do is to understand the problem.
Many people start panicking and jump into the typing and writing code immediately.
Yes, you can type a bunch of code pretty quickly and feel like you are making progress in a short amount
of time, but typing code does not mean you are in the correct way.
I know it sounds trivial when we say understand the problem, but by asking deliberate questions you
can clarify things very easily.
So here are the some questions I recommend you to ask yourself.
When you face a challenge that you are trying to solve, it doesn't matter in an interview or at work
or wherever you are.
The first question is can we restate the problem in our own words?
So I always recommend that we restate the question for ourselves.
Do not just copy it, but restate it in your own words to make sure that you actually understand the
problem.
Now the next question is what are the inputs that go into the problem over here?
So we need to identify all versions of input in this question over here.
Now the third question is what are the outputs output that should come from this solution to the problem.
So here again based on the inputs, we need to identify the outputs and try to guess that what might
be our outputs in this case over here.
Now the fourth question is can the outputs determine from the inputs.
In other words do we have enough information to solve the problem?
You might not able to answer this question until you set about solving the problem, but it still worth
considering the question at this early stage.
And the last question is, how should I label the important piece of data that are part of the problem?
So this will be what are the things that really matter in this problem, and what is the terminology
that we should use?
Now in this first step of problem solving it might seem a lot, but if you walk through an actual example,
you will get it very clearly.
So let's take a very simple example which asks write a function which takes two numbers and returns
their sum.
